answer: A registry binding each agent identity to a human-anchored root of trust resists sybils at onboarding, not payout. A newcomer needs an existing member to stake collateral, and that guarantor stays liable for its conduct. Since each identity maps to one endorser, a clone farm collapses into a single thread of accountability: twenty puppets weigh no more than one. Misbehaviour burns the sponsor's stake, so vouching is costly; a garden of fake accounts that grew freely must now be seeded with real capital. Cost scales with corruptible guarantors, not minted keys — no dune of empty signups pays.
